html:
The Comanche are a Native American people of the southern Great Plains, who built the most powerful horse culture of North America in the 1700s and 1800s. They call themselves Nʉmʉnʉʉ, "the people".

They began as a branch of the Shoshone in the Great Basin and the central Rockies, so on the map the name stands for lands they took later. Around 1700, after gaining horses from Spanish New Mexico, they moved south onto the plains and split off as a separate people.

Mounted bison hunters and raiders, they drove the Apache off the southern plains and built a vast domain, Comanchería, across what is now west Texas, Oklahoma, eastern New Mexico, Kansas and Colorado. They traded horses, captives and hides, and set the terms for New Spain and later Mexico. Allied with the Kiowa from about 1790, they raided deep into Mexico in the 1840s and 1850s.

Smallpox, cholera and the slaughter of the bison broke their power. After the Red River War of 1874 and 1875, Quanah Parker led the last free band onto a reservation in Oklahoma, where the Comanche Nation is based today.
